matthew/7.meaning: Bad or harmful; the same word can mean 'the evil one.' It appears in the Lord's Prayer: 'deliver us from evil.'
Originally a stage actor playing a part. Jesus uses it for religious performance with no heart behind it.
What is taught, or the act of teaching. Crowds are astonished at the authority of Jesus' teaching.

matthew/8.meaning: To go after someone as a disciple. The typical call of Jesus: 'Follow me.'
matthew/8.gloss: To go after as a disciple

matthew/8.meaning: Used for waking from sleep, getting up and being raised from the dead, which is why healing and resurrection language overlap in the Gospels.
The absence of light, used for ignorance, evil and separation from God. It is the opposite of light in John.

matthew/9.meaning: To go without food for a spiritual purpose. Jesus assumes his followers will fast but warns against doing it for show.
A person known for flagrant sin or living outside respectable religion. Jesus is repeatedly criticized for eating with them.
Literally 'missing the mark.' Sin as a failure, a wrong done, and a power that holds people.

discussion.matthew/1: Matthew's genealogy includes Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Bathsheba, women with complicated stories. What point do you think he is making about the family Jesus comes from?
discussion.matthew/2: Herod's experts knew exactly where the Messiah would be born, yet only foreign Magi went to look. Why do you think the people closest to the answer didn't move?
discussion.matthew/3: John calls the Pharisees and Sadducees a "brood of vipers" even though they came to be baptized. What do you think he saw in them that drew such a harsh response?
discussion.matthew/4: Satan quotes Psalm 91 in the second temptation, and Jesus answers with another verse rather than arguing. What does that exchange show about how each of them is using Scripture?
discussion.matthew/5: Jesus ends a run of "You have heard it said… but I say to you" with "Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect." What do you think he is doing to his listeners' sense of what the law asks?
discussion.matthew/6: Jesus says people who pray and give to be seen "have received their reward." What do you think he means by that reward, and why would it be a poor one?
discussion.matthew/7: Jesus warns that some who call him "Lord, Lord" will be turned away. Why do you think the Sermon ends on such a sobering note?
discussion.matthew/8: Jesus is asleep in the boat while the disciples panic, then asks, "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?" What do you think he expected of them in that moment?
discussion.matthew/9: After Matthew's dinner with tax collectors, the Pharisees question the disciples instead of Jesus. Why do you think they went to the disciples?
discussion.matthew/10: Before sending out the Twelve, Jesus warns that they will be hated and dragged before courts. Why do you think he is so blunt about what lies ahead?
discussion.matthew/11: John, in prison, sends to ask, "Are you the one who is to come?" Why do you think John asks, and why does Jesus answer by pointing to what he is doing?
discussion.matthew/12: The Pharisees say Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebul. What does Jesus' reply about a divided kingdom show about why their accusation doesn't hold together?
discussion.matthew/13: The disciples ask why Jesus speaks in parables, and he quotes Isaiah about people who hear but do not understand. Do you think the parables are meant to reveal or to conceal?
discussion.matthew/14: Herod was "sorry" about his promise to Herodias' daughter, yet had John beheaded anyway. What do you think kept him from doing otherwise?
discussion.matthew/15: The Pharisees complain that the disciples don't wash their hands, and Jesus answers by pointing to "Corban" and honoring parents. Why do you think he shifts the argument there?
discussion.matthew/16: Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, and within minutes Jesus calls him "Satan." What do you think Peter misunderstood about the Messiah?
discussion.matthew/17: Peter offers to build three tents on the mountain, and a cloud interrupts him with "Listen to him." Why do you think the voice answers Peter this way?
discussion.matthew/18: Peter asks if forgiving seven times is enough, and Jesus tells of a servant forgiven a huge debt who then chokes a fellow servant over a small one. Why couldn't the first servant pass the mercy along?
discussion.matthew/19: The rich young man says he has kept the commandments yet asks, "What do I still lack?" Why do you think Jesus' answer sent him away sorrowful?
discussion.matthew/20: The workers hired first complain when everyone receives the same wage. What do you think the owner's reply, "Are you envious because I am generous?", is meant to show?
discussion.matthew/21: The crowd shouts "Hosanna" as Jesus enters, yet the city asks, "Who is this?" Why do you think the welcome was both so loud and so uncertain?
discussion.matthew/22: The Pharisees and Sadducees keep testing Jesus, and then he asks them a question about David's Lord. What do you think he is showing them about their view of the Messiah?
discussion.matthew/23: Jesus piles up seven woes on the scribes and Pharisees, then laments over Jerusalem. How do you think the sorrow in that lament changes how we read the anger?
discussion.matthew/24: The disciples ask for the sign of Jesus' coming, and he answers with warnings instead of dates. What do you think he wants them to focus on instead?
discussion.matthew/25: In the sheep and goats scene, both groups are surprised: "When did we see you?" Why do you think neither group realized it?
discussion.matthew/26: Jesus tells Peter he will deny him three times, and Peter swears he never will. Why do you think Peter was so sure of himself?
discussion.matthew/27: Pilate washes his hands and says, "I am innocent of this man's blood." Do you think the gesture clears him, and why does Matthew include it?
discussion.matthew/28: Matthew says that even as the eleven worshiped Jesus, "some doubted." Why do you think he includes that detail just before the Great Commission?
discussion.mark/1: Jesus repeatedly tells demons, the healed and a leper to keep quiet about him. Why do you think Mark's Jesus wants silence so early in the story?
discussion.mark/2: When four friends tear open a roof, Jesus begins with "Your sins are forgiven." Why do you think he started there, and what are the scribes thinking in their hearts?
discussion.mark/3: Jesus' family comes to take charge of him, saying, "He is out of his mind." What do you think they feared, and why does Mark set this beside the scribes' accusation?
discussion.mark/4: Jesus explains the parables privately to the disciples and says the secret of the kingdom "has been given" to them. What do you think separates the insiders from the outsiders in this chapter?
discussion.mark/5: The man freed from Legion begs to go with Jesus and is told to go home and tell his story. Why do you think Jesus sent him back instead of letting him follow?
discussion.mark/6: Mark says Herod was "greatly perplexed" by John yet liked to listen to him, then had him beheaded. What do you think was going on inside Herod?
discussion.mark/7: Jesus quotes Isaiah: "This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me." What exactly do you think he is accusing the Pharisees of?
discussion.mark/8: Jesus heals a blind man in two stages, right before Peter's confession. Why do you think Mark placed that slow healing there?
discussion.mark/9: After the disciples fail to cast out a demon, the boy's father says, "I believe; help my unbelief!" Why do you think Jesus responds to such a mixed prayer?
discussion.mark/10: James and John ask for seats at Jesus' right and left right after he predicts his death a third time. What does that tell you about what they were hearing?
discussion.mark/11: Mark wraps the cleansing of the temple inside the story of the cursed fig tree. How do you think the two events explain each other?
discussion.mark/12: After the parable of the tenants who kill the owner's son, the leaders want to arrest Jesus but do not. What do you think held them back, and what had they understood?
discussion.mark/13: When the disciples admire the temple, Jesus says its stones will be thrown down, and four of them ask when. Why do you think he answers with warnings about being deceived instead of a timeline?
discussion.mark/14: A young man flees naked when Jesus is arrested, and Peter denies him three times. Why do you think Mark includes such unflattering details about the followers?
discussion.mark/15: Mark says Pilate knew the priests had handed Jesus over "out of envy," yet he gave in to the crowd. What do you think Pilate was weighing?
discussion.mark/16: Mark's earliest ending has the women flee in fear and say nothing to anyone. Why do you think the Gospel ends so abruptly, and what might it be asking of readers?
discussion.luke/1: Zechariah asks, "How can I know this?" and is struck silent, while Mary asks, "How can this be?" and is called blessed. What do you think distinguishes the two questions in Luke's telling?
discussion.luke/2: At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple and says, "Did you not know I must be in my Father's house?" What do you think Mary and Joseph did and did not understand?
discussion.luke/3: Luke places Jesus' baptism beside a genealogy ending "son of Adam, son of God." Why do you think he traces the line all the way back there?
discussion.luke/4: In his hometown synagogue Jesus is first praised, then nearly thrown off a cliff. What in his words about Elijah and Elisha turned the crowd?
discussion.luke/5: After the huge catch, Peter falls at Jesus' knees and says, "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man." Why do you think the miracle made him say that?
discussion.luke/6: Jesus follows "Blessed are you who are poor" with "Woe to you who are rich." What do you think the blessings and woes are doing in his speech?
discussion.luke/7: The centurion sends friends because he doesn't feel worthy to come, yet Jesus says he has not found such faith in Israel. What do you think Jesus recognized in him?
discussion.luke/8: After Jesus heals the man with the legion of demons, the townspeople ask him to leave. Why do you think they respond with fear instead of joy?
discussion.luke/9: Peter calls Jesus "the Christ of God," and Jesus immediately says he must suffer and be killed. Why do you think he follows the confession with that prediction?
discussion.luke/10: In the Good Samaritan story, the priest and the Levite pass by on the other side. What reasons might they have had, and why does Jesus make the hero a Samaritan?
discussion.luke/11: Jesus is accused of casting out demons by Beelzebul and answers with the strong man who is overpowered by a stronger one. What do you think the story says about who is in charge?
discussion.luke/12: God calls the rich man "You fool," though he only planned for a good harvest. What do you think is the key detail in the parable that makes him foolish?
discussion.luke/13: Jesus says the Galileans killed by Pilate and the people crushed by the tower were no worse sinners than others, then tells of a fig tree. How do you think the parable answers what people were asking?
discussion.luke/14: In the banquet parable the invited guests all make excuses, and the host fills the hall with the poor and outsiders. What do you think the excuses are really saying?
discussion.luke/15: The older brother refuses to go in, the father goes out to plead with him, and the story ends there. Why do you think Jesus leaves it unresolved?
discussion.luke/16: Abraham tells the rich man that his brothers have Moses and the Prophets and would not be convinced even if someone rose from the dead. What is Jesus saying about what it takes for people to believe?
discussion.luke/17: Ten lepers are cleansed, and the one who returns to give thanks is a Samaritan. Why do you think Luke points that out?
discussion.luke/18: The tax collector goes home justified rather than the Pharisee. What would Jesus' first listeners, who admired Pharisees, have thought of this ending?
discussion.luke/19: Zacchaeus climbs a tree, and the crowd grumbles that Jesus is staying with a sinner. Why do you think Jesus chose to go to his house, and what happens before anyone asks Zacchaeus to change?
discussion.luke/20: When the leaders try to trap Jesus about taxes, he asks for a coin first. What do you think the image on the coin has to do with his answer?
discussion.luke/21: Right after the widow's gift, the disciples admire the temple stones and Jesus says they will be thrown down. Why do you think Luke places those two scenes together?
discussion.luke/22: Jesus tells Peter, "I have prayed for you," knowing he will deny him, and after the rooster crows Jesus looks at him. What do you think Peter heard in that prayer and that look?
discussion.luke/23: One criminal mocks Jesus while the other asks to be remembered. What do you think changed the second man's view of the man beside him?
discussion.luke/24: The two on the Emmaus road don't recognize Jesus until he breaks bread, then say their hearts burned as he opened the Scriptures. Why do you think Luke tells the story this way?
discussion.john/1: John calls Jesus "the Word" who was with God and was God. Why do you think he begins his Gospel this way instead of with a birth story?
discussion.john/2: Mary tells Jesus, "They have no wine," and he answers, "My hour has not yet come," then acts anyway. Why do you think he responds that way?
discussion.john/3: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night and then fades from the conversation. Why do you think John mentions the time, and what is Nicodemus missing?
discussion.john/4: When Jesus brings up her husbands, the Samaritan woman changes the subject to where to worship. Why do you think she does that, and why does Jesus follow her there?
discussion.john/5: A man who has waited thirty-eight years answers Jesus' question with an excuse. What do you think is going on in his answer?
discussion.john/6: After the Bread of Life teaching many disciples leave, and Jesus asks the Twelve, "Do you want to go away as well?" What does Peter's answer show about why he stays?
discussion.john/7: Jesus' brothers urge him to go public in Judea, yet John says they did not believe in him. What do you think motivated their advice?
discussion.john/8: The scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery but not the man. What do you think they were really trying to do, and what might Jesus' silence be doing?
discussion.john/9: The healed man's parents answer the Pharisees evasively: "Ask him; he is of age." Why do you think they stepped back from their own son?
discussion.john/10: Jesus calls himself both the gate and the good shepherd. Why do you think he uses two images, and who are the thieves and hired hands?
discussion.john/11: Jesus waits two days before going to Bethany, and both Martha and Mary say, "If you had been here." Why do you think he delayed?
discussion.john/12: Judas objects to Mary's anointing, and John adds that Judas used to steal from the money bag. Why do you think John tells us that detail?
discussion.john/13: Peter protests the foot washing, then asks Jesus to wash his hands and head too. What do you think he misunderstood at first, and what changed?
discussion.john/14: Philip says, "Show us the Father," and Jesus answers, "Have I been with you so long, and you still do not know me?" What do you think Philip was missing?
discussion.john/15: Jesus says the Father is the vinedresser who prunes every branch. Why do you think he describes the Father's role this way, and what does the pruning accomplish in the picture?
discussion.john/16: Jesus tells the disciples he is going away, and they grow sad instead of asking where. Why do you think he says it is "to your advantage" that he go?
discussion.john/17: Jesus prays for the disciples, then for "those who will believe through their word." Why do you think he spends so much of the prayer on unity?
discussion.john/18: Pilate asked, "What is truth?" and went out without waiting for an answer. Did Pilate not want to know the answer to his own question?
discussion.john/19: Pilate has "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews" written above the cross, and the chief priests object. Why do you think the sign mattered so much to both sides?
discussion.john/20: Thomas says he won't believe unless he sees and touches the wounds, and Jesus invites him to do exactly that. Why do you think Jesus granted the request instead of rebuking him?
discussion.john/21: Jesus asks Peter three times, "Do you love me?" and Peter is grieved. Why do you think Jesus asks three times, and what might Peter be hearing?

discussionShort.matthew/1: Why does Matthew list Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Bathsheba in Jesus' family tree?
discussionShort.matthew/2: Why did only foreign Magi go to look, when Herod's experts knew where the Messiah would be born?
discussionShort.matthew/3: Why does John call the Pharisees a "brood of vipers" when they came to be baptized?
discussionShort.matthew/4: What does Satan quoting Psalm 91, and Jesus' reply, show about using Scripture?
discussionShort.matthew/5: What is Jesus doing to our sense of the law when he says, "Be perfect"?
discussionShort.matthew/6: What reward have those who pray to be seen "received," and why is it a poor one?
discussionShort.matthew/7: Why does the Sermon end with some who say "Lord, Lord" being turned away?
discussionShort.matthew/8: Why does Jesus ask the panicking disciples, "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?"
discussionShort.matthew/9: Why did the Pharisees question the disciples rather than Jesus himself?
discussionShort.matthew/10: Why is Jesus so blunt that the Twelve will be hated and dragged to court?
discussionShort.matthew/11: Why does John ask, "Are you the one?", and why does Jesus answer by pointing to his deeds?
discussionShort.matthew/12: How does Jesus' "divided kingdom" reply expose the problem with the Beelzebul charge?
discussionShort.matthew/13: Are the parables meant to reveal or to conceal?
discussionShort.matthew/14: Herod was "sorry" yet had John beheaded. What kept him from doing otherwise?
discussionShort.matthew/15: Why does Jesus shift the handwashing argument to honoring parents?
discussionShort.matthew/16: What did Peter misunderstand about the Messiah, to be called "Satan" so soon after his confession?
discussionShort.matthew/17: Why does the voice answer Peter's tent offer with "Listen to him"?
discussionShort.matthew/18: Why couldn't the forgiven servant pass his master's mercy along?
discussionShort.matthew/19: Why did Jesus' answer send the rich young man away sorrowful?
discussionShort.matthew/20: What is "Are you envious because I am generous?" meant to show?
discussionShort.matthew/21: Why was the "Hosanna" welcome so loud, yet the city's response so uncertain?
discussionShort.matthew/22: What does Jesus' question about David's Lord show about their view of the Messiah?
discussionShort.matthew/23: How does Jesus' lament over Jerusalem change how we read the seven woes?
discussionShort.matthew/24: Why does Jesus answer a request for a sign with warnings instead of dates?
discussionShort.matthew/25: Why were both the sheep and the goats surprised: "When did we see you?"
discussionShort.matthew/26: Why was Peter so sure he would never deny Jesus?
discussionShort.matthew/27: Does Pilate's hand-washing clear him, and why does Matthew include it?
discussionShort.matthew/28: Why does Matthew say "some doubted" just before the Great Commission?
discussionShort.mark/1: Why does Mark's Jesus keep demanding silence so early in the story?
discussionShort.mark/2: Why does Jesus begin with "Your sins are forgiven" for the man on the mat?
discussionShort.mark/3: Why does Mark place the family's fear beside the scribes' accusation?
discussionShort.mark/4: What separates the insiders from the outsiders in the parables?
discussionShort.mark/5: Why does Jesus send the healed man home instead of letting him follow?
discussionShort.mark/6: Herod liked listening to John yet had him killed. What was going on inside him?
discussionShort.mark/7: What is Jesus accusing the Pharisees of with Isaiah's "lips" and "heart"?
discussionShort.mark/8: Why does Mark place the two-stage healing right before Peter's confession?
discussionShort.mark/9: Why does Jesus respond to "I believe; help my unbelief"?
discussionShort.mark/10: What were James and John hearing when they asked for thrones just after the death prediction?
discussionShort.mark/11: How do the fig tree and the temple cleansing explain each other?
discussionShort.mark/12: What held the leaders back from arresting Jesus after the parable of the tenants?
discussionShort.mark/13: Why does Jesus answer "When?" with warnings about being deceived?
discussionShort.mark/14: Why does Mark include the fleeing young man and Peter's denials?
discussionShort.mark/15: What was Pilate weighing, knowing the priests acted "out of envy"?
discussionShort.mark/16: Why does Mark end with the women's silent fear, and what does that ask of readers?
discussionShort.luke/1: How do Zechariah's and Mary's "how" questions differ in Luke's telling?
discussionShort.luke/2: What did Mary and Joseph not understand about "my Father's house"?
discussionShort.luke/3: Why does Luke trace Jesus' line back to "son of Adam, son of God"?
discussionShort.luke/4: What in Jesus' words about Elijah and Elisha turned the crowd?
discussionShort.luke/5: Why did the miracle make Peter say, "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man"?
discussionShort.luke/6: What are the blessings and woes doing in Jesus' speech?
discussionShort.luke/7: What did Jesus recognize in the centurion that he hadn't found in Israel?
discussionShort.luke/8: Why do the townspeople respond to the healing with fear, not joy?
discussionShort.luke/9: Why does Jesus follow Peter's confession with a prediction of suffering?
discussionShort.luke/10: Why make the hero a Samaritan, and what excuses might the priest and Levite have had?
discussionShort.luke/11: What does the strong man parable say about who is really in charge?
discussionShort.luke/12: What detail in the parable makes the rich man a "fool"?
discussionShort.luke/13: How does the fig tree parable answer what people asked about the tragedies?
discussionShort.luke/14: What are the invited guests' excuses really saying?
discussionShort.luke/15: Why does Jesus leave the older brother's story unresolved?
discussionShort.luke/16: What does Abraham's answer say about what it takes for people to believe?
discussionShort.luke/17: Why does Luke point out that the thankful leper was a Samaritan?
discussionShort.luke/18: How would Jesus' first listeners have reacted to the tax collector going home justified?
discussionShort.luke/19: Why did Jesus go to Zacchaeus' house before anyone asked him to change?
discussionShort.luke/20: What does the image on the coin have to do with Jesus' answer?
discussionShort.luke/21: Why does Luke put the widow's gift right next to the temple's coming fall?
discussionShort.luke/22: What did Peter hear in Jesus' prayer, and in the look after the rooster crowed?
discussionShort.luke/23: What changed the second criminal's view of the man beside him?
discussionShort.luke/24: Why does Luke tie the recognition to the breaking of bread and the opened Scriptures?
discussionShort.john/1: Why does John begin with "the Word" instead of a birth story?
discussionShort.john/2: Why does Jesus answer Mary with "my hour has not yet come," then act anyway?
discussionShort.john/3: Why does John mention it was night, and what is Nicodemus missing?
discussionShort.john/4: Why does the woman change the subject, and why does Jesus follow her there?
discussionShort.john/5: What is going on in the man's excuse after thirty-eight years?
discussionShort.john/6: What does Peter's "To whom shall we go?" show about why he stays?
discussionShort.john/7: What motivated the advice of Jesus' brothers, who didn't believe in him?
discussionShort.john/8: Why bring the woman but not the man, and what is Jesus' silence doing?
discussionShort.john/9: Why did the man's parents step back with "Ask him; he is of age"?
discussionShort.john/10: Why two images, the gate and the shepherd, and who are the thieves and hired hands?
discussionShort.john/11: Why did Jesus delay two days, and why do both sisters say, "If you had been here"?
discussionShort.john/12: Why does John tell us Judas used to steal from the money bag?
discussionShort.john/13: What did Peter misunderstand at first, and what changed his mind?
discussionShort.john/14: What was Philip missing when he said, "Show us the Father"?
discussionShort.john/15: Why does Jesus describe the Father as the vinedresser who prunes?
discussionShort.john/16: Why is it "to your advantage" that Jesus goes away?
discussionShort.john/17: Why does Jesus spend so much of his prayer on unity?
discussionShort.john/18: Did Pilate not want to know the answer to his own question, "What is truth?"
discussionShort.john/19: Why did the sign over the cross matter so much to both Pilate and the priests?
discussionShort.john/20: Why did Jesus grant Thomas' request instead of rebuking him?
discussionShort.john/21: Why does Jesus ask Peter three times, and what might Peter be hearing?
